message.content:
The sculpture most often cited as the quintessential icon of the 19th‑century art world is **“The Thinker” by Auguste Rodin**.  
Rodin conceived the figure in 1880, and it was first cast in bronze in 1902, but the original marble version (1881–1885) and its later bronze editions became emblematic of modern sculpture. Its contemplative pose, dramatic musculature, and psychological depth captured the spirit of the era’s artistic revolution, making it the most celebrated and widely reproduced sculpture of the 1800s.
